text: It's three in the morning, in an emergency room

So her family has to have the hardest
conversation of their lives, all over again
In India, ninety-eight percent of people with advanced
cancer don't get the palliative care they need
Yes, you heard that right
Ninety-eight
That's why we built Sahara
It's an app for people with cancer
and for the families who look after them
We're five people who met at Health-a-thon
Basith and Awaiz run a software company called WeDevIT
Dr Sujay is from IISc, Bengaluru
Dr Sharada is from AIIMS, Mangalagiri

Back in August, we had our first team meeting

Patients do tell you what they want at the end of life
But nobody writes it down

So we did what technical people do
We built everything
Screen after screen, all for doctors
Then we asked ourselves one question
Why would a family install all this?
So we pivoted, towards the patient and the family
And we kept one thing at the centre: the goals of care talk
That's when the doctor, the patient and the family sit
down together, and decide what kind of care she wants
With everyone's consent, the doctor records that talk
AI writes out who said what
For Indian languages, we use Sarvam AI
Then the AI checks that nothing important was missed
It goes through thirteen topics
taken from India's end-of-life care guidelines
written by the national critical
care and palliative care societies
Then the AI turns the conversation
into a goals of care document

Does she want CPR?
A ventilator?
Intensive care?
And where does she want to be cared for?
Nothing is final until the doctor
reads it, corrects it, and signs it
Then the family signs too, and it's locked
We also took legal advice on the
wording and the format of that document
But goals of care is only the start
Sahara stays with the family, every single day
Patients track their symptoms
They rate how they're feeling on a distress thermometer
and they mark where it hurts on a body map

There's a mood journal, for the days
that are hard to put into words
They take a photo of a prescription, or a medicine strip
AI works out the medicines
and reminds them about every dose
They upload their reports
and ask a question in plain words
AI answers, and shows the exact
line in the report it came from
Their next hospital visit is scheduled right in the app
Family members get their own login
so everyone stays in the loop
There's an emergency SOS button

wishes, contacts and medicines
We also scraped public listings
and put over sixteen hundred

And there's a community
so no family goes through this alone
Families don't talk in just one language
